text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has introduced price increases on petroleum products of between seven and nine percent.
- A giant coal-fired power plant in southwest Turkey is emptying waste directly into the Aegean Sea.
- The businessmen's association, TUSIAD, accepted its first member from Diyarbakir in the troubled southeast.
- The government is faced with a shortage of teachers after extending complusory education from five to eight years at the weekend. Retired teachers will be encouraged to return to work.
- The tactics of Islam-based Welfare Party, having lost the education debate in parliament, will be to mount protests throughout the country.
- Sales of Turkey's Hayat bottled water have greatly increased since entering into a partnership with the French Danone company.
- The foreign ministry has increased efforts to improve Turkey's human rights situation ahead of a visit by a European Union Human Rights Commission.
- Tansu Ciller's conservative opposition True Path Party is split by whether to apply to the constitutional court alongside the Islamists to try to overturn the new education law.
- Since the new government took power at the end of June, there have been continual price rises on everything from fuel to plane tickets and tea.
